questions.question: In 2017, who became the first Indian singer to make it to Delhi's Madame Tussauds Museum?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shreya Ghoshal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In 2017, **Shreya Ghoshal** became the first Indian singer to have her wax statue installed at **Madame Tussauds Museum in Delhi**.
 
• The statue of Shreya Ghoshal was unveiled in the museum’s Bollywood music zone, recognizing her contributions to Indian playback singing.
 
• Shreya Ghoshal is a renowned playback singer, known for lending her voice to numerous hit songs across various Indian languages.
 
• She has won multiple national awards and Filmfare awards, cementing her legacy as one of India’s most celebrated singers.
 
• Her wax figure at Madame Tussauds represents her immense popularity and the influence she holds in the Indian music industry.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Madame Tussauds Museum:**

 
 
• It is a chain of wax museums, originally founded by Marie Tussaud in London in 1835.
 
• The museum is famous for creating lifelike wax figures of celebrities, historical figures, and cultural icons from around the world.
 
• The Delhi branch of Madame Tussauds opened in 2017 and features statues of Bollywood stars, sports personalities, and other Indian icons.
 
 
 
• **Shreya Ghoshal:**
 
 
• She debuted in Bollywood playback singing with the movie *Devdas* (2002), for which she won the National Film Award for Best Female Playback Singer.
 
• She has recorded songs in over 20 Indian languages, including Hindi, Bengali, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, and Malayalam.
 
• Known for her versatility, Shreya has sung in genres ranging from classical to contemporary music.
 
 
 
• **Wax Sculpting Process:**
 
 
• The process of creating a wax statue involves detailed measurements, photography, and consultations with the subject (if alive).
 
• It may take several months to complete a single figure, using high-quality wax and materials to achieve lifelike accuracy.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Madame Tussauds:**
 
 
• Having a wax statue in Madame Tussauds is considered a major recognition of global popularity and influence.
 
• Indian personalities like Mahatma Gandhi, Amitabh Bachchan, Sachin Tendulkar, and now Shreya Ghoshal have been honored with statues at various branches of the museum.

questions.question: Vitamin D is synthesised using sunshine, by the:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**skin**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The skin synthesizes Vitamin D when exposed to ultraviolet B (UVB) radiation from sunlight.
 
• Vitamin D synthesis occurs when 7-dehydrocholesterol in the skin absorbs UVB light, converting it into pre-vitamin D3, which is then transformed into active Vitamin D (calcitriol) in the liver and kidneys.
 
• Approximately 10–30 minutes of sun exposure, a few times a week, is sufficient for most people to produce adequate Vitamin D levels, depending on skin type and geographical location.
 
• The process is influenced by factors such as time of day, season, latitude, skin pigmentation, and sunscreen usage.
 
• Vitamin D plays a crucial role in calcium absorption, bone health, immune function, and overall well-being.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **7-dehydrocholesterol:** A precursor molecule found in the skin that absorbs UVB radiation to initiate Vitamin D synthesis.
 
• **Calcitriol (Active Vitamin D):** The biologically active form of Vitamin D, which is essential for maintaining calcium and phosphate homeostasis in the body.
 
• **Deficiency Risks:** Lack of sufficient sunlight exposure or dietary intake can lead to Vitamin D deficiency, causing rickets in children and osteomalacia in adults.
 
• **Dietary Sources:** While sunlight is the primary source, Vitamin D can also be obtained from foods like fatty fish, egg yolks, fortified dairy products, and supplements.
 
• **UVB Radiation:** A type of ultraviolet light with wavelengths between 280–315 nm, critical for Vitamin D production but also associated with the risk of skin damage and cancer if overexposed.

questions.question: As on 31st October 2023, the youngest member of parliament (in terms of age) in the 17th Lok Sabha, Chandrani Murmu, represents which political party?

__
 
• Chandrani Murmu is the youngest Member of Parliament (MP) in the 17th Lok Sabha, elected at the age of 25.
 
• She represents the **Biju Janata Dal (BJD)**, a regional political party based in Odisha.
 
• She was elected from the **Keonjhar constituency** in Odisha during the 2019 general elections.
 
• Chandrani Murmu is the first woman MP from Keonjhar and one of the youngest MPs in India’s parliamentary history.
 
• Her election highlighted the growing representation of young leaders in Indian politics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• BJD is a regional political party in Odisha, founded in 1997 by Naveen Patnaik.
 
• The party is named after Naveen Patnaik's father, Biju Patnaik, a prominent freedom fighter and former Chief Minister of Odisha.
 
• BJD has a strong presence in Odisha and focuses on regional development and welfare policies.
 
 
 
• **17th Lok Sabha:**
 
 
• The 17th Lok Sabha was constituted following the 2019 general elections in India.
 
• It marked a significant rise in the number of women MPs, with 78 women elected, the highest in Indian history.
 
 
 
• **Women in Indian Politics:**
 
 
• India has seen a gradual increase in women’s participation in politics, though gender representation remains uneven.
 
• Efforts like reservation for women in local governance (Panchayati Raj) have paved the way for greater involvement.
 
 
 
• **Odisha in Indian Politics:**
 
 
• Odisha has played a significant role in Indian politics, with leaders like Biju Patnaik and Naveen Patnaik shaping its political landscape.

questions.question: The institution like Lokpal or Lokayukta (Ombudsman) was first created in which of the following countries?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sweden**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The institution of Ombudsman (Lokpal/Lokayukta) was first established in **Sweden** in 1809.
 
• The Swedish word "Ombudsman" translates to "representative" or "agent," and the role was created to safeguard citizens' rights by addressing public grievances against administrative actions.
 
• The Swedish Ombudsman is independent of the government and reports directly to the Parliament, ensuring transparency and accountability.
 
• Sweden's Ombudsman system inspired similar institutions worldwide, including the Lokpal in India and Lokayuktas in Indian states.
 
• The concept of Ombudsman emphasizes the importance of democratic accountability and the protection of citizens' rights against administrative injustices.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lokpal and Lokayukta Act, 2013 (India):**

 
 
• The Lokpal is a central anti-corruption body in India, established under the Lokpal and Lokayukta Act, 2013, to investigate complaints against public officials.
 
• Lokayuktas are similar institutions functioning at the state level to address corruption and maladministration.
 
 
 
• **Key Characteristics of Ombudsman:**
 
 
• An Ombudsman is an independent and impartial authority, generally appointed to address public grievances.
 
• The institution acts as a mediator between the state and its citizens, ensuring fairness in administrative processes.
 
 
 
• **Global Influence:**
 
 
• Many countries have adopted the Ombudsman system, modifying it to suit their governance structures, including the UK, Canada, Australia, and India.
 
• The Ombudsman concept promotes accountability and transparency in governance globally.
 
 
 
• **Modern Variants:**
 
 
• In addition to traditional Ombudsman roles, specialized variants have emerged, such as Banking Ombudsman, Insurance Ombudsman, and Consumer Ombudsman, to address sector-specific grievances.
 
• These institutions cater to the evolving needs of modern societies, ensuring justice in specialized domains.

questions.question: Which of the following structures has the IUPAC name 7-hydroxy-5-methylheptan-2-one?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The IUPAC name "7-hydroxy-5-methylheptan-2-one" refers to a structure with a hydroxyl (-OH) group on carbon 7, a methyl (-CH3) group on carbon 5, and a ketone (>C=O) group on carbon 2.
 
• In IUPAC nomenclature, the longest continuous carbon chain is chosen as the parent chain, and substituents are numbered to give the lowest possible locants.
 
• Option 2 correctly represents the structure where the functional groups are located as per the name: hydroxyl at position 7, methyl at position 5, and ketone at position 2.
 
• The numbering begins from the end closest to the ketone group, ensuring it gets the smallest locant (2).
 
• The name adheres to IUPAC conventions, ensuring clarity and standardization in chemical representation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **IUPAC Nomenclature:** It is the standardized system for naming chemical compounds, ensuring consistency across scientific communication globally.
 
• **Functional Groups:** Hydroxyl (-OH), methyl (-CH3), and ketone (>C=O) are common groups that dictate the chemical properties and reactivity of organic compounds.
 
• **Locants:** Numbers assigned to substituents or functional groups indicate their positions on the parent chain in the molecular structure.
 
• **Ketones:** Ketones are organic compounds characterized by the carbonyl group (>C=O) bonded to two carbon atoms. They are commonly used in industry and biological systems.
 
• **Hydroxy Compounds:** Compounds containing hydroxyl groups (-OH) are classified as alcohols or phenols, depending on their structural context, and play a key role in chemical synthesis and biological processes.

questions.question: Which of the following was the capital of Vatsa Mahajanapada?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kausambi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Vatsa Mahajanapada was one of the sixteen Mahajanapadas in ancient India, mentioned in Buddhist and Jain texts.
 
• Kausambi was the capital city of Vatsa, situated near the modern-day location of Kosam on the Yamuna River in Uttar Pradesh.
 
• The city was a significant center for trade and governance during the Mahajanapada period.
 
• Kausambi was renowned for its prosperity and served as a hub for economic activities and cultural exchanges.
 
• Udayana, a famous ruler of Vatsa, ruled from Kausambi and is known for his association with early Buddhist traditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mahajanapadas:** These were sixteen great kingdoms or oligarchic republics that existed in ancient India during the 6th century BCE.
 
• **Location of Vatsa:** Vatsa was situated in the central region of present-day Uttar Pradesh, near the Yamuna River.
 
• **Significance of Kausambi:** The city was fortified and developed as a major urban center with excellent infrastructure and trade networks.
 
• **Udayana:** He was a prominent king of Vatsa who played a key role in promoting Buddhism and was mentioned in several Buddhist texts.
 
• **Trade and Cultural Exchange:** Kausambi was an important node for trade routes, facilitating interactions between different regions of ancient India.

questions.question: In June 2023, which state government among the following has announced the 'Shakti' scheme for free bus travel for women and trans people within the state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Karnataka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Karnataka government launched the 'Shakti' scheme in June 2023 to provide **free bus travel for women and trans individuals** within the state.
 
• The initiative is part of the newly elected Congress government's **five key poll promises (Pancha Sutras)**.
 
• Under the scheme, women and trans persons can avail of **free travel on state-run buses**, excluding luxury and air-conditioned buses.
 
• The scheme is aimed at empowering women and promoting **gender inclusivity** while reducing the financial burden of transportation.
 
• Beneficiaries need to present a valid government-issued ID to avail of free bus services under this scheme.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pancha Sutras:** These are the five key guarantees promised by the Karnataka Congress government, including free bus travel for women, 200 units of free electricity (Gruha Jyoti), monthly financial assistance (Gruha Lakshmi), unemployment benefits (Yuva Nidhi), and free ration distribution (Anna Bhagya).
 
• **State-run buses:** The scheme covers buses operated by Karnataka State Road Transport Corporation (KSRTC) and Bangalore Metropolitan Transport Corporation (BMTC), excluding luxury and premium services.
 
• **Gender inclusivity:** By including trans individuals, the Shakti scheme emphasizes **social equity and inclusiveness**.
 
• **Economic impact:** This initiative is expected to improve the mobility of women, enabling them to access education, employment, and healthcare services more effectively.
 
• **Implementation:** The scheme is funded by the state government, which has allocated a significant budget to ensure its smooth rollout and maintenance.

questions.question: According to Article ____ no religious instruction shall be provided in any educational institution wholly maintained out of State funds.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**28**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 28** of the Indian Constitution prohibits the provision of religious instruction in any educational institution wholly maintained out of State funds.
 
• However, there is an exception for institutions established under endowments or trusts that mandate the provision of religious instruction.
 
• The prohibition under Article 28 ensures secularism and the separation of religion from state-funded educational institutions.
 
• This article is part of the larger framework of **Fundamental Rights**, specifically under the "Right to Freedom of Religion" (Articles 25-28).
 
• The aim is to ensure that no state-funded institution forces or promotes any specific religious instruction, maintaining neutrality in matters of religion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Secularism in India:** India follows a model of positive secularism, meaning all religions are treated equally, and the state does not favor or discriminate against any religion.
 
• **Exceptions in Article 28:** Religious instruction is allowed in institutions established under specific religious endowments or trusts, provided participation in such instruction is voluntary.
 
• **Other Related Articles:**
 
 
• **Article 25:** Ensures freedom of conscience and the right to freely profess, practice, and propagate religion.
 
• **Article 26:** Grants every religious denomination the right to manage its religious affairs.
 
• **Article 27:** Prohibits the use of tax proceeds for promoting or maintaining any particular religion.
 
 
 
• **Educational Institutions in India:** The categorization includes state-funded, privately funded, and minority institutions. Only state-funded institutions are subject to the restrictions of Article 28.
 
• **Judicial Interpretation:** The Supreme Court of India has upheld Article 28's provisions as a critical element of India's secular framework in cases such as *S.R. Bommai v. Union of India (1994)*.

questions.question: Which structure within the nucleus contains genetic information in the form of DNA?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chromosome**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Chromosomes** are thread-like structures located within the nucleus of cells that house genetic material.
 
• Each chromosome is composed of DNA tightly coiled around proteins called histones, forming a compact structure.
 
• Humans typically have 23 pairs of chromosomes, including one pair of sex chromosomes (XX or XY).
 
• Chromosomes contain genes, which are segments of DNA responsible for encoding proteins and determining traits.
 
• The genetic information stored in chromosomes is essential for cell division, growth, and reproduction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **DNA (Deoxyribonucleic Acid):** DNA is the molecule that carries genetic instructions for the development, functioning, growth, and reproduction of all living organisms and viruses.
 
• **Histones:** These are proteins that help in the packaging of DNA into structural units called nucleosomes, facilitating the compaction of chromosomes.
 
• **Nucleus:** The nucleus is the organelle within eukaryotic cells that houses chromosomes and regulates gene expression and cell division.
 
• **Gene:** A gene is a functional unit of heredity, consisting of a sequence of DNA that encodes a specific protein or RNA molecule.
 
• **Cell Division:** During processes like mitosis and meiosis, chromosomes replicate and segregate to ensure genetic material is passed to daughter cells accurately.

questions.question: Which of the following is the first planned industrial city in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jamshedpur**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Jamshedpur**, located in the state of Jharkhand, is the first planned industrial city in India.
 
• It was established by the visionary industrialist **Jamsetji Tata** in 1919 to serve as a hub for the Tata Steel Company.
 
• The city was designed by architect **Frederick Litchfield**, with well-planned infrastructure for industrial and residential areas.
 
• Jamshedpur is often referred to as **“Steel City”** or **“Tata Nagar”** due to its association with Tata Steel, one of the largest steel producers in India.
 
• The city is a pioneer in urban planning in India, featuring wide roads, efficient drainage systems, and designated industrial zones.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Industrial City Concept:**

 
 
• An industrial city is a planned urban area designed to cater to manufacturing and industrial activities.
 
• It includes infrastructure like factories, warehouses, and residential areas for workers.
 
 
 
• **Jamsetji Tata:**
 
 
• The founder of the Tata Group, he envisioned Jamshedpur as an industrial hub for India's economic growth.
 
• He laid the foundation for Tata Steel, Asia’s first integrated steel plant.
 
 
 
• **Urban Planning in Jamshedpur:**
 
 
• The city has a unique layout with separate zones for industries, housing, and recreational areas.
 
• It is managed by the Tata Steel Utilities and Infrastructure Services Limited (formerly JUSCO).
 
 
 
• **Significance of Jamshedpur:**
 
 
• The city is a center for steel production, contributing significantly to India's industrial output.
 
• It has won awards for cleanliness and urban management, making it a model for other industrial towns.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a commercial bank?

options.text: The Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation of India Bank
National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **NABARD** is a development bank established for promoting sustainable and equitable agriculture and rural development in India.
 
• It was set up on **12 July 1982**, based on the recommendations of the B. Sivaraman Committee.
 
• NABARD focuses on providing credit, refinancing, and other facilities to support rural development projects, rather than functioning as a commercial bank.
 
• Unlike commercial banks, NABARD does not accept deposits from individuals or offer regular banking services like savings accounts or loans to the general public.
 
• Commercial banks, such as the State Bank of India (SBI) and ICICI Bank, serve individual customers and businesses with a variety of banking products and services.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Commercial Banks**:

 
 
• These are financial institutions that provide a variety of banking services, such as accepting deposits, offering loans, and facilitating transactions.
 
• Examples include the State Bank of India (SBI), ICICI Bank, and the Development Bank of Singapore (DBS).
 
• They cater to individual customers, businesses, and corporations.
 
 
 
• **NABARD's Role**:
 
 
• It primarily acts as a refinancing institution for rural credit and aids in the development of rural infrastructure.
 
• NABARD partners with state governments, NGOs, and banks to implement projects related to rural development.
 
• It focuses on sectors like irrigation, rural housing, and agricultural productivity.
 
 
 
• **Difference Between Commercial and Development Banks**:
 
 
• Commercial banks serve the general public, while development banks like NABARD focus on specific sectors, such as agriculture and rural infrastructure.
 
• Development banks do not offer conventional banking services like savings accounts or credit cards.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Development Banks in India**:
 
 
• National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD).
 
• Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI).
 
• Export-Import Bank of India (EXIM Bank).

questions.question: Who among the following received the Nritya Kalanidhi for the year 2022?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bragha Bessell**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Bragha Bessell, a renowned Bharatanatyam dancer and teacher, was honored with the prestigious Nritya Kalanidhi award for the year 2022.
 
• Nritya Kalanidhi is an esteemed recognition awarded by the Music Academy Madras to outstanding performers in the field of Bharatanatyam.
 
• Bragha Bessell is widely recognized for her emotive abhinaya (expressive storytelling) and contributions to the art form.
 
• She has trained numerous students and has played a pivotal role in preserving and propagating Bharatanatyam globally.
 
• The award reflects her dedication and lifetime achievement in Indian classical dance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nritya Kalanidhi Award:**

 
 
• The Nritya Kalanidhi is a prestigious honor conferred annually by the Music Academy Madras, focusing on excellence in Bharatanatyam.
 
• This award is part of the institution's efforts to celebrate and promote classical dance.
 
 
 
• **Bharatanatyam:**
 
 
• Bharatanatyam is one of the oldest classical dance forms in India, originating from Tamil Nadu.
 
• It is characterized by intricate footwork, expressive gestures, and storytelling through abhinaya.
 
• The dance form is deeply rooted in spiritual themes, often depicting tales from Hindu mythology.
 
 
 
• **Music Academy Madras:**
 
 
• Founded in 1928, the Music Academy Madras is one of India's premier institutions for Carnatic music and classical dance.
 
• It hosts the annual December Music Season, a globally renowned festival showcasing Indian classical arts.
 
 
 
• **Abhinaya in Bharatanatyam:**
 
 
• Abhinaya refers to the art of expression in Indian classical dance, encompassing facial expressions, gestures, and emotions.
 
• It is a crucial element in Bharatanatyam, enabling dancers to convey intricate narratives and spiritual themes.
 
• Bragha Bessell is celebrated for her mastery in abhinaya, making her performances deeply impactful.

questions.question: In which of the following years was a Hindu College in Benaras established to impart education from the ancient Sanskrit texts?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1791**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Hindu College in Benaras was established in **1791** by Jonathan Duncan, a British officer.
 
• The objective of the college was to promote the study of **Sanskrit texts and traditional Indian knowledge systems**.
 
• It was one of the earliest institutions in India to focus on **preserving and imparting classical Sanskrit education**.
 
• The institution later evolved into the **Government Sanskrit College** and played a critical role in the education system of the region.
 
• The establishment of the college was part of the British efforts to understand and govern Indian society better by studying its ancient texts and traditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jonathan Duncan:** He was the British Resident in Benaras and initiated the establishment of the Hindu College to promote the study of Indian classical knowledge and culture.
 
• **Sanskrit Education:** Sanskrit was considered the language of ancient Indian scriptures, including the Vedas, Upanishads, and other philosophical texts.
 
• **Benaras (Varanasi):** Known as a center of learning and spirituality in India, Varanasi has been a hub for education and cultural preservation for centuries.
 
• **Impact on Higher Education:** The Hindu College laid the groundwork for future educational institutions that focused on blending traditional Indian education with modern methodologies.
 
• **Transition to Modern Institutions:** The college's legacy contributed to the establishment of institutions such as Banaras Hindu University (BHU), which continues to be a major center for higher education in India today.

questions.question: Which festival is celebrated at Sabarimala temple, on the occasion of Makar Sakranti?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Makara Vilakku**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Makara Vilakku** is a significant festival celebrated at the Sabarimala temple in Kerala, marking the culmination of the Mandala-Makaravilakku pilgrimage season.
 
• The festival is observed on **Makara Sankranti**, which usually falls on January 14th, coinciding with the sun's transition to the zodiac sign of Capricorn (Makara).
 
• The highlight of the festival is the **appearance of the sacred light (Makara Jyothi)** on the Ponnambalamedu hill, which is considered auspicious by devotees.
 
• It is a seven-day festival that attracts millions of pilgrims from across India, emphasizing devotion to Lord Ayyappa, the presiding deity of Sabarimala.
 
• Makara Vilakku symbolizes the union of celestial and spiritual energies, celebrated with rituals, prayers, and offerings at the temple.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lord Ayyappa:** The deity worshipped at Sabarimala is Lord Ayyappa, considered a symbol of unity between Vaishnavism and Shaivism. He is believed to be the son of Lord Shiva and Mohini (an incarnation of Lord Vishnu).
 
• **Makara Jyothi:** The sacred light seen on the Ponnambalamedu hill during Makara Sankranti is considered divine by devotees. While some believe it to be a celestial phenomenon, others regard it as a ritualistic lamp lit by temple authorities.
 
• **Mandala Pooja:** The 41-day Mandala Pooja, observed by pilgrims before visiting Sabarimala, involves strict austerities like celibacy, vegetarianism, and wearing a black or blue attire.
 
• **Sabarimala Temple:** Located in the Periyar Tiger Reserve, Sabarimala is one of the largest annual pilgrimage sites in the world, with a tradition of welcoming devotees irrespective of caste, creed, or religion.
 
• **Rituals and Practices:** Pilgrims chant "Swamiye Saranam Ayyappa" (Ayyappa is our refuge) and carry the "Irumudi Kettu" (a sacred bundle) as an offering to Lord Ayyappa during their trek to the temple.

questions.question: Former Indian actress Vyjayanthimala was trained in which classical dance form?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bharatanatyam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Vyjayanthimala**, a former Indian actress, was an accomplished classical dancer trained in **Bharatanatyam**.
 
• Bharatanatyam is one of the **oldest classical dance forms of India**, originating in Tamil Nadu.
 
• Vyjayanthimala was known for integrating her expertise in Bharatanatyam into her film performances, setting her apart in the Indian film industry.
 
• Her training in Bharatanatyam was under the guidance of **Guru Vazhuvoor Ramiah Pillai**, a renowned figure in the Vazhuvoor tradition of the dance form.
 
• She was instrumental in popularizing Bharatanatyam in mainstream Indian cinema and emphasized its artistic and cultural significance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bharatanatyam**:

 
 
• It is a classical dance form that combines **expression (bhava)**, **melody (raga)**, **rhythm (tala)**, and **drama (natya)**.
 
• Traditionally performed in temples as a form of devotional offering to deities, Bharatanatyam is deeply rooted in Indian spiritual traditions.
 
• The dance form is characterized by intricate footwork, graceful hand gestures (mudras), and elaborate facial expressions.
 
• Bharatanatyam's theoretical foundation is based on the **Natyashastra**, an ancient treatise on performing arts attributed to Bharata Muni.
 
 
 
• **Vyjayanthimala's Contribution:**
 
 
• Apart from her acting career, Vyjayanthimala performed Bharatanatyam on international stages, promoting Indian culture globally.
 
• She also conducted workshops and lectures to educate audiences about the art form's history and significance.
 
 
 
• **Vazhuvoor Tradition:**
 
 
• This is one of the traditional schools (banis) of Bharatanatyam, known for its soft and graceful movements.
 
• The Vazhuvoor style emphasizes storytelling through expressive abhinaya (facial expressions) and fluid postures.
 
 
 
• **Recognition:**
 
 
• Vyjayanthimala received several awards for her contributions to Indian art and cinema, including the **Padma Shri** and other accolades.
 
• Her dedication to Bharatanatyam earned her a lasting legacy in the field of Indian classical dance.

questions.question: Who among the following was the first sultan of Delhi Sultanate to visit the Ajmer shrine of Khwaja Muinuddin Chishti?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Muhammad bin Tughlaq**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Muhammad bin Tughlaq** was the first Sultan of the Delhi Sultanate to visit the Ajmer shrine of Khwaja Muinuddin Chishti.
 
• He ruled the Delhi Sultanate from **1325 to 1351** and was the second ruler of the Tughlaq dynasty.
 
• Muhammad bin Tughlaq had a deep interest in Sufism and is known for his patronage of Sufi saints.
 
• The Ajmer shrine, also known as the **Dargah of Khwaja Muinuddin Chishti**, is a prominent pilgrimage site for followers of Sufism and Islam.
 
• The visit symbolized the Sultan’s respect for the Chishti Sufi order, which played a significant role in the spiritual and cultural history of medieval India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Khwaja Muinuddin Chishti:**

 
 
• He was a renowned Sufi saint and founder of the Chishti Order in India.
 
• Known as "Gharib Nawaz" (Benefactor of the Poor), his teachings emphasized love, tolerance, and openness.
 
• His dargah in Ajmer is one of the most significant Sufi shrines in the world.
 
 
 
• **Sufism in India:**
 
 
• Sufism is the mystical dimension of Islam, focusing on inner spirituality and devotion to God.
 
• The Chishti Order was one of the most prominent Sufi orders in medieval India, emphasizing service to humanity.
 
 
 
• **Muhammad bin Tughlaq’s Reign:**
 
 
• He is often remembered for his ambitious but failed projects, including the transfer of the capital from Delhi to Daulatabad.
 
• His administration was marked by a mix of innovation and impracticality.
 
 
 
• **Delhi Sultanate:**
 
 
• The Delhi Sultanate (1206–1526) was a Muslim kingdom based in Delhi that ruled over large parts of the Indian subcontinent.
 
• It was established after the defeat of the Rajput ruler Prithviraj Chauhan by Muhammad Ghori in the Second Battle of Tarain.

questions.question: In which year was Pt. Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (Scheme) announced by the Government of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2014**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Pt. Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDU-GKY) was announced in **2014** by the Government of India.
 
• The scheme is a part of the National Rural Livelihood Mission (NRLM) and aims to **enhance the employability of rural youth**.
 
• It primarily targets **rural poor youth in the age group of 15-35 years**, focusing on skill development and employment generation.
 
• The program is implemented under the **Ministry of Rural Development** (MoRD).
 
• DDU-GKY is linked with the "Make in India" and "Skill India" initiatives to **support rural development and economic growth**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Skill Development:** DDU-GKY aims to enhance skill training for rural youth to make them industry-ready and economically independent.
 
• **Placement-Linked:** The scheme mandates that at least 70% of the trained candidates should be placed in jobs with a minimum wage.
 
• **Special Focus:** Priority is given to socially disadvantaged groups such as women, Scheduled Castes (SC), Scheduled Tribes (ST), and minorities.
 
• **Funding Model:** The program follows a Public-Private Partnership (PPP) model where training is conducted by Project Implementing Agencies (PIAs).
 
• **Global Reach:** DDU-GKY also has provisions to train and place candidates in overseas jobs, enhancing international employment opportunities.

questions.question: In Kerala and coastal area of Karnataka the pre-monsoon shower is known as ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mango**____** Shower**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Mango showers** are **pre-monsoon rainfall** occurring in **Kerala and coastal Karnataka**.
 
• They usually occur in **April–May**, before the onset of the **South-West Monsoon**.
 
• These showers help in the **early ripening of mangoes**, hence the name.
 
• They are important for **horticulture and agriculture**, especially mango orchards.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kalbaisakhi:** These are pre-monsoon thunderstorms that occur in West Bengal, Odisha, and Assam during March-May, also known as Nor'westers.
 
• **Bardoisila:** A local term used in Assam for strong pre-monsoon winds and rains, named after a mythical spirit.
 
• **Mango Showers:** Pre-monsoon rains in Kerala and Karnataka that aid in the ripening of mangoes, distinct from Blossom Showers.
 
• **Southwest Monsoon:** The primary monsoon season in India, lasting from June to September, bringing significant rainfall to most parts of the country.
 
• **Impact on Agriculture:** Pre-monsoon showers like Blossom and Mango Showers are critical for crop yield, including coffee, mangoes, and other regional crops.

questions.question: According to the Human Development Index 2023-24, what is the rank of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**134**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• India ranks **134th** in the **Human Development Index (HDI) 2023-24**, as reported by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP).
 
• The HDI is a composite index measuring average achievement in three basic dimensions: **health (life expectancy), education, and standard of living (GNI per capita)**.
 
• India's HDI score for the year is approximately **0.633**, indicating medium human development.
 
• Countries are classified into four development categories: **low, medium, high, and very high human development**, with India positioned in the medium development category.
 
• India's ranking reflects progress in areas such as education and health but highlights challenges in reducing inequality and improving income distribution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Human Development Index (HDI)**

 
 
• Introduced in 1990 by the UNDP, HDI is used to rank countries based on human development levels.
 
• The index combines **life expectancy, mean years of schooling, expected years of schooling**, and **Gross National Income (GNI) per capita**.
 
• The higher the HDI value, the greater the level of human development in a country.
 
 
 
• **India's HDI Progress**
 
 
• India has shown improvement over the years, particularly in education and healthcare sectors.
 
• However, challenges persist in areas such as gender inequality and regional disparities.
 
 
 
• **Global HDI Trends**
 
 
• Countries like Norway, Switzerland, and Iceland consistently rank in the top positions with very high HDI scores.
 
• Sub-Saharan African and South Asian countries often rank lower due to challenges in healthcare, education, and income.
 
 
 
• **Impact of COVID-19 on HDI**
 
 
• COVID-19 led to setbacks in global human development progress, particularly in health and education sectors.
 
• Countries are working towards recovery by investing in healthcare systems and educational reforms.

questions.question: Plutonic rocks are formed when lava cools ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**in the crust**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Plutonic rocks**, also known as intrusive igneous rocks, are formed when magma cools and solidifies **below the Earth's surface**, specifically in the crust.
 
• The slow cooling of magma allows the formation of large, visible **mineral crystals** in plutonic rocks.
 
• Common examples of plutonic rocks include **granite, diorite, and gabbro**, which are extensively used in construction and decorative purposes.
 
• Plutonic rocks are exposed to the surface over time due to **erosion and tectonic uplift**.
 
• The term "plutonic" is derived from Pluto, the Roman god of the underworld, symbolizing their formation deep within the Earth's crust.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Igneous rocks** are classified into two main types based on their formation: **intrusive (plutonic)** and **extrusive (volcanic)**.
 
• Intrusive rocks form **beneath the Earth's surface**, while extrusive rocks form **on the surface** when lava cools quickly.
 
• The cooling rate of magma determines the texture of igneous rocks—**slow cooling forms coarse-grained rocks**, while rapid cooling forms fine-grained rocks.
 
• Plutonic rocks are often associated with **large geological features** such as batholiths, laccoliths, and dikes.
 
• Understanding plutonic rocks helps geologists study the Earth's **interior processes, tectonics, and mineral resources**.

questions.question: Drains exiting from Mohenjo-Daro had ______ doors that were probably closed at night to prevent vagrants or negative elements from entering the city through that access.

__
 
• The drains of Mohenjo-Daro were equipped with **wooden doors**, which were likely used to secure the city at night.
 
• Mohenjo-Daro, part of the ancient Indus Valley Civilization, had an advanced drainage system demonstrating urban planning expertise.
 
• The wooden doors on drains were designed to prevent access by vagrants or harmful elements, ensuring the city's safety and hygiene.
 
• Wood was a commonly used material in the Indus Valley Civilization for construction purposes, including doors and other structures.
 
• This feature reflects the civilization's emphasis on maintaining order and security within their urban settlements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mohenjo-Daro:** It is one of the largest cities of the Indus Valley Civilization, located in present-day Pakistan.
 
• **Drainage System:** The Indus Valley cities had a sophisticated drainage system, with covered drains made of bricks running along the streets.
 
• **Urban Planning:** Mohenjo-Daro was laid out in a grid pattern, indicating advanced town planning methods for its time.
 
• **Material Use:** Wood, along with mud bricks and baked bricks, was extensively used in construction within the civilization.
 
• **Security Measures:** The presence of wooden doors on drains highlights the civilization's awareness of safety and urban management challenges.
